note: Structured restatement of the three DGF cases as they are described in the manuscript. Page locators refer to the printed pagination of Canale (2026), Security Architect Survival Kit. Framework facts are separated from this paper's analytical additions. Nothing in this file is a measurement.

framework.title: Security Architect Survival Kit: Role, Expectations and Journey within the Digital Governance Framework (DGF)
framework.author: Jeremy Canale

supplier_platform.note: Security precedes IT only on this route

framework_facts: SaaS CRM serving 2,000 sales users; confidential customer data
Backup restoration untested; recovery-time objective undefined

conditions: MFA and recovery conditions before go-live

W1_new_platform.analytical_handoff_design: Table of W1 contracts in the manuscript (this paper's addition)

framework_facts: Own on-premises Active Directory, cloud mail, provider-hosted ERP
Payroll motivates a request for network interconnection within 30 days
Account inventories absent; a past incident undocumented; EDR missing; logs local

framework_outcome.exception: filtered partner-zone connection during the audit, without joining directories
conditions: risk card signed by the integration director
directories joined only after the audit

W2_ma_integration.analytical_handoff_design: Table 3 of the manuscript (this paper's addition, not a measured deployment)

parameter_mapping.kappa: undocumented incident: expensive to investigate before any automation (baseline selection)
parameter_mapping.eta: missing provider reports: an agent cannot create absent evidence; discovering gaps can inflate exception effort
parameter_mapping.mu: conditions register with the EDR precondition and the 30- and 60-day obligations (ordinary-path review)
parameter_mapping.B_A: integration playbooks, routing rules and agent evaluations maintained whatever the number of acquisitions

framework_facts: Internal IT-support agent built with Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry)
Reads tickets and SharePoint through its integrations; accesses Microsoft Graph
Uses the developer's identity and service principal
No prompt or action logs; retrieval across the whole SharePoint index
W3_new_internal_project.analytical_handoff_design: Table 4 of the manuscript (this paper's addition; later rows apply only if a revised design proceeds)

parameter_mapping.kappa: the rejected design is an exception whose baseline effort is already high
parameter_mapping.mu: comparing declared with actual permissions is standard-path work; its review ratio depends on how far the tests can be trusted
parameter_mapping.B_A: keeping the assessed agent separate from the reviewing agents adds identity and monitoring work

risk_scale.rule: ordinal impact (1-4) x ordinal likelihood (1-4); 12-16 is critical and calls for rejection or competent governance arbitration; above-tolerance acceptance requires a business risk owner and a dated acceptance record
risk_scale.caveat: the ordinal product is not an expected monetary loss

generic_routes.note: Illustrative orders used in the manuscript. The 'paths' entry above records the orders of the practitioner framework; enterprises define their own gates, orders and tasks.
